_comment: Adjudicated repairs for Functions. Cleanest chapter of the source so far — all keys verified correct; defects are equivalent-value option pairs and loose wording. Every entry re-derived by hand.

01-11.reason: Option C read 'a horizontal line x = 5' — internally inconsistent (x = 5 is vertical). Corrected to 'vertical', which keeps it a genuine non-function distractor; key B (upward parabola) retained.

01-35.reason: Options A (9) and B (9/1) were numerically identical. B replaced; key A retained (f(4) = 9/1 = 9).

01-40.reason: Options A ([0,∞)−{4}) and the keyed C ([0,4)∪(4,∞)) denoted the same set. A replaced with a strict subset (false); key C retained (need x ≥ 0 and x ≠ 4).

01-46.reason: Options A (3) and B (9/3) were numerically identical. B replaced; key A retained (g(7) = 9/3 = 3).

04-26.reason: Doubly duplicated set: A ≡ C (1/(x+1) vs 1/(1+x)) and B ≡ D. C and D replaced with distinct false forms; key A retained (f(1/x) = (1/x)/((1/x)+1) = 1/(1+x)).

05-7.reason: Options A (x²−2x+1) and D ((x−1)²) were identical. D replaced with the wrong-sign square; key A retained.

05-8.reason: Options A (2) and C (ln(e²)) were equivalent. C replaced; key A retained (ln(e²) = 2).

05-24.reason: Options A (4) and D (e^{2ln2}) were equivalent. D replaced with the exponent itself (≈1.39, false); key A retained ((e^{ln2})² = 4).

05-26.reason: Options A (1) and C (tan(π/4)) were equivalent, and D's '\sqrt[1]{π/4}' was a typeset oddity. C replaced with tan(π/3) = √3 (false), D cleaned to π/4; key A retained.

05-32.reason: Options B (4) and D (log₂16) were equivalent. D replaced; key B retained ((f∘g)(3) = log₂(2⁴) = 4).

05-37.reason: Options A (3) and B (√9) were equivalent. B replaced; key A retained (√(2·4+1) = 3).

05-38.reason: Options A (1) and C (cot(π/4)) were equivalent. C replaced; key A retained (cot(π/2 − π/4) = 1).

05-42.solution: \(\sec(\arccos x) = \frac{1}{x}\). \(\arccos\) needs \(x \in [-1, 1]\), and at \(x = 0\), \(\arccos 0 = \frac{\pi}{2}\) where \(\sec\) is undefined — so the domain is \([-1, 1] \setminus \{0\}\).
05-42.reason: No printed option matched the true domain [−1,1]−{0} (sec fails at arccos 0 = π/2). Keyed option B repaired from (−1,1); key B retained.

05-45.reason: Options A (9/5) and B (18/10) were the same value unreduced. B replaced with a false fraction; key A retained (f(9) = 18/10 = 9/5).

06-26.reason: C (10/1) duplicated the keyed B (10) and D (5/1) duplicated A (5). Both replaced with distinct values; key B retained (solve (2y+1)/(y−3) = 3 ⇒ y = 10).

06-35.reason: Options A ((x−1)/x) and C (1 − 1/x) were the identical inverse. C replaced with a false form; key A retained (y = 1/(1−x) ⇒ x = (y−1)/y).

02-2.stem: Which of the following function types is defined by: distinct elements of the domain always map to distinct elements of the codomain?
02-2.reason: As printed ('every element maps to a unique element') the property describes EVERY function, not injectivity. Stem reworded to the actual defining property; key A (one-to-one) retained.

02-37.reason: Options B (piecewise x / −x) and D (|x|) both described the modulus function — equivalent distractors. D replaced with a distinct false step function; key A (the true sgn definition) retained.

02-40.reason: Old option A ('one-to-one but not onto ℝ') was ALSO a true statement (codomain-dependent), making two defensible answers. Replaced with a false claim (|x| = x is injective on [0,∞)); key C retained.

02-44.reason: Old option B ('Onto') was ALSO true — x³ − x is surjective on ℝ — making two correct options. Replaced with a false claim (the cubic is unbounded); key C (odd function) retained.

02-46.reason: Old option D ('bijective on (0,∞)') was arguably also true (1/x is a self-inverse bijection there). Pinned to a false codomain claim (1/x never attains 0); key B (odd) retained.
